scenes.text: An ostrich's eyes are so big that together, they're bigger than its brain.
Each eye is about two inches across, roughly the size of a billiard ball.
That makes them the biggest eyes of any land animal.
Its brain, meanwhile, is only about the size of a walnut.
Those giant eyes give it sharp long-distance vision on the open plains.
And the rest of the bird is just as extreme.
Ostriches are the biggest birds alive, up to nine feet tall and over three hundred pounds.
They can't fly, but they can sprint at about forty-three miles per hour.
A single stride can cover three to five meters.
They have only two toes on each foot, while most birds have three or four.
Their wings work like rudders, helping them turn and brake at full speed.
They also lay the biggest bird eggs, about six inches across.
And no, they don't bury their heads in the sand.
They lower their heads to turn their eggs in shallow nests in the ground, which can look that way from far off.
Which ostrich fact surprised you the most? Tell me below.

title: An ostrich's eyes are bigger than its brain 👀
caption: Ostriches have the biggest eyes of any land animal, about 2 inches across, and together they're bigger than their walnut-sized brain. Plus: 43 mph sprints and only 2 toes.
